heading: 8.1 Same dimension — valid, auto-converted
text:
### 8.1 Same dimension — valid, auto-converted [LUNI.8.1]

`+`, `-`, `%` and the comparisons between values of the same physical dimension
are valid; the compiler converts both operands to the dimension's base unit
before combining, at compile time when an operand is a literal and at runtime
otherwise.

`/` and `//` between values of the same dimension are valid too, and need no
annotation. The compiler converts both operands the same way, and the result is a
bare number ([LUNI.8.3]): `/` is a `Float` ([LEXP.7.4]) and `//` follows the
operand rule ([LEXP.7.5]). A `unit scalar` group ([LUNI.4.2]) is a dimension for
this clause. The other operators are [LUNI.8.4]'s.
